assumptions: Each salary payment belongs to one family member — the "who paid it" you mentioned is the family member the salary is for.
Each salary payment goes into one of your bank accounts, and you record which one each time.
You lend money to family members, and your brother is one of them.
You are the one lending the money, so a loan does not need to record who lent it.
A loan can be paid back in several smaller amounts over time.
The categories you listed are examples, and you can add more categories over time.
How much your brother still owes is worked out from each loan and his repayments, so nothing about it is stored separately.
